2607.05880.title: Harrison.Rad 1.5 Technical Report: A radiology foundation model that can draft reports from images, priors and clinical context
2607.05880.paper_summary: Imaging demand is growing faster than the radiology workforce can expand, and reporting backlogs cannot be resolved through training and recruitment alone. The most direct opportunity is reducing the time and effort radiologists spend producing reports, a task that requires interpreting images, integrating clinical history and prior studies, and drafting structured findings. We present Harrison.Rad 1.5 (HR1.5), a radiology-specific multimodal large language model that accepts interleaved text and visual inputs and generates structured and unstructured text across plain-film radiology, spanning computed radiography, chest, musculoskeletal, abdominal, spine, and pelvic x-rays, and mammography. HR1.5 is trained through a three-stage pipeline: domain adaptation of a base language model on radiology reports, contrastive vision-encoder training with curriculum-based hard negatives on ~6 million image-report instances, and visual-question-answering fine-tuning on multi-turn conversations. We evaluate it with a Findings-Diagnosis scoring framework that extends RadGraph-XL entity extraction with ontology-based synonym matching and polarity-contradiction detection, benchmarked on RadBench, a simulated FRCR 2B Short Case examination scored against Angoff-method thresholds, ReXGradient, and internal multi-modality datasets. HR1.5 is the only system evaluated to meet the simulated FRCR passing standard and achieves the highest accuracy on closed-format clinical questions, across anatomical regions, on internal multi-body-part and mammography reporting, and on the primary clinically-aligned score for public chest reporting. We further examine explainability and model behaviour, including question-sensitive Grad-CAM heatmaps, attention analysis, and confidence estimation, to support responsible future evaluation toward clinical use, and a framework for clinically grounded assessment of report quality.
2607.05880.paper_summary_zh: 影像需求的增長速度超過了放射科工作人員的擴展速度，報告的積壓無法僅通過培訓和招聘來解決。最直接的機會是減少放射科醫生在生成報告上花費的時間和精力，這項任務需要解釋影像、整合臨床歷史和先前的研究，並草擬結構化的發現。我們介紹Harrison.Rad 1.5 (HR1.5)，這是一種專門針對放射科的多模態大型語言模型，能夠接受交錯的文本和視覺輸入，並生成結構化和非結構化文本，涵蓋平片放射學，包括計算放射學、胸部、肌肉骨骼、腹部、脊椎和骨盆X光，以及乳腺攝影。HR1.5通過三個階段的流程進行訓練：對放射報告的基礎語言模型進行領域適應，使用基於課程的困難負樣本進行對比視覺編碼器訓練，涵蓋約600萬個影像-報告實例，以及在多輪對話中進行視覺問題回答的微調。我們使用一個發現-診斷評分框架來評估它，該框架擴展了RadGraph-XL實體提取，並結合基於本體的同義詞匹配和極性-矛盾檢測，基準測試在RadBench上，這是一個模擬的FRCR 2B短案例考試，根據Angoff方法的標準進行評分，ReXGradient，以及內部多模態數據集。HR1.5是唯一一個被評估以符合模擬FRCR通過標準的系統，並在封閉格式的臨床問題上達到最高準確率，涵蓋解剖區域，在內部多身體部位和乳腺攝影報告上，以及在公共胸部報告的主要臨床對齊分數上。我們進一步檢查可解釋性和模型行為，包括對問題敏感的Grad-CAM熱圖、注意力分析和信心估計，以支持對臨床使用的負責任未來評估，以及一個針對報告質量的臨床基礎評估框架。
